title: Could Homework Widen the Gap Between Families?
paragraphs: Homework is a normal part of primary school in many countries, and parents are usually expected to help their children with it. A new study from the University of Manchester, published in the British Journal of Sociology of Education, suggests that this habit may make educational differences between families bigger.

The researchers describe a case study of one mother, Emma, and one teacher. The first author of the paper was a parent at the school. Emma works until 8 in the evening, so it is hard for her to find time. Families with more time, knowledge and money can help more, and they can pay for private tutoring if they need it.

The authors also warn that schools may read a parent's lack of time as a lack of commitment. This can make some parents feel ashamed or stressed. However, the study is small, so it cannot prove that the same is true everywhere. The authors add that simply removing homework might not help, because other kinds of parent involvement could take its place.

questions.q: What does the study say about homework?
questions.a: It may make differences between families bigger.

questions.q: Why is it hard for Emma to help?
questions.a: She works until 8 in the evening.

questions.q: Why can we not say the result is true everywhere?
questions.a: The study is small: it follows only one mother and one teacher.
